brief: True round barn about 60 ft in diameter, built on a wheat farm as an experiment in efficient feeding: a low cylindrical wall of pale-painted horizontal siding with a ring of small square windows and a pair of white-braced X-pattern hinged doors, under a tall self-supporting bell-shaped (bowed gambrel) dome roof of dark wood shingles rising to a small round ventilator cupola at the peak. It sits at the bottom of a curving plowed slope below the farmstead's gable-roofed house, sheds and a windbreak of spruce.
